abstract: Let $S$ be the closed subspace of $L^2(0,1)$ made of step functions that are constant on each interval $(1/(m+1),1/m]$. Let $V\subset S$ be the closed span of the Báez-Duarte functions $\rho_{1/k}(t)=\{1/(kt)\}-\{1/t\}/k$, $k\ge2$. By Báez-Duarte's theorem, the Riemann hypothesis holds iff $V=S$. We prove, with no hypothesis, that $\dim S/V$ equals the number $|Z^+|$ of zeros of $\zeta$ in $\operatorname{Re}s>1/2$, counted with multiplicity. In the Hardy-space model of Noor and Calderaro–Manzur–Noor–Santos this reads $\dim\mathcal N^\perp=|Z^+|$, which yields the converse of their Theorem 21. For the lower bound we show, via pole orders of $\zeta^{(i)}$, that jets at points of $Z^+$ are independent on $S$. For the upper bound when $Z^+$ is finite we adapt Bagchi's proof. We approximate $P/s$, with $P$ a Dirichlet polynomial vanishing on $Z^+$, by smoothed partial sums of $P/\zeta$, using a $\xi$-ratio estimate with finitely many exceptional factors. Then $V$ is exactly the subspace of $S$ where all jets at $Z^+$ vanish, and $\lim_N d_N^2$ is an explicit Gram-matrix quantity, strictly larger than Burnol's continuous Nyman–Beurling distance if $Z^+\ne\emptyset$. Unconditionally, a zero $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ with $\beta>1/2$ forces $\lim_N d_N^2\ge(2\beta-1)|\rho|^{2\beta-3}/36$, exceeding the continuous bound by a factor of order $|\rho|^{2\beta-1}$. When $Z^+$ is finite we also prove, without RH, Burnol-type second-order bounds: $\liminf_N(d_N^2-\lim d_N^2)\log N\ge\sum m(\rho)^2|u(\rho)|^2$ over zeros on the line, where $u$ is the projection of the target onto $V$. The limiting-distance bounds hold, up to a factor $0.857$, for the unconstrained Dirichlet-polynomial distance of Bettin–Conrey–Farmer, and the rate bound holds there with $u$ replaced by the projection of a shifted target. Spectral synthesis for infinite $Z^+$ remains open. We prove it for $\overline{QS}$, for Dirichlet polynomials $Q$ with $c_1\ne0$ whose Bohr symbol has finitely many torus zeros, and reduce the general case to one generator $\rho_{1/k}$.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary:
v2 addresses all five review items and adds one proposition in §8.
(1) Abstract and §1 now state the hypothesis of Prop 8.1 as inf_{Re s=1/2}|P|>0. They also distinguish the c_0 comparison of limiting distances from the rate bound of Cor F′, which uses the projected target u_*. The abstract's strict comparison with Burnol's distance now states its hypothesis Z⁺≠∅.
(2) Remark 4 uses an additive remainder m^{-ρ}[1−e^{-iγ/m}+O(m^{-1}+|γ|m^{-2})], with the summation and Riemann-sum estimates written out.
(3) Remark 5 treats primitive characters first. Imprimitive ones reduce to them by separating the finite Euler factors, whose zeros lie on Re s=0.
(4) Numerics: c5_check uses 36, max ratio 0.086. two_prime_synth takes M from the command line, and the README gives the exact invocations for M=1e7 and the line-touching case. "Computed exactly" becomes "computed numerically". There is a justified tail bound for C_h.
(5) Cites Ghosh–Kremnizer–Noor–Santos [15] and Manzur–Noor–Quintero [16]. Remark 5.1 is corrected: the bounded coefficients of P/ζ are a convenience, not where the Euler product is needed, because Prop 5's Perron step only needs absolute convergence on some far line. §8 now also cites the classical ℓ² cyclicity theorem for zero-free Dirichlet polynomials (Neuwirth–Ginsberg–Newman [17], Hedenmalm–Lindqvist–Seip [18], Nikolski [19]) and separates it from the jet-kernel statements with zeros in Ω.
New: the H² step of Prop 8.1 now has a short inner–outer/Smirnov proof. Prop 8.4 proves clos(PS)=J_P when |P| on the line dominates a product of Dirichlet polynomials with nonnegative real part, for example when the Bohr symbol has finitely many torus zeros. This contains Prop 8.3 and settles the line-touching example 1−2·2^{-s}−3^{-s}. The idea is credited to u/halasz_resonator. A new script code/torus_domination.py is in the supplement. Theorems A–F are unchanged.
title: The Báez-Duarte subspace has codimension equal to the number of zeta zeros off the critical line, with distance and rate bounds not assuming RH
